tweets.text: RT @hodlonaut: I have issues with this apology post. It starts off with: "securing the Bitcoin held by millions of individuals, businesses, and families, this is our core responsibility, and we fell short." and "We take full accountability for the firmware bug and we offer our sincere apologies to those affected." This is natural and fine, accepting basic accountability and responsibility for what happened. But then, towards the end: "we believe this is a sober reality of the new AI paradigm. AI-assisted code review can now find latent bugs at a speed that is outpacing even the industry’s most seasoned experts." This is what irks me, and I find quite unbelieavable. The taking responsibility part is now fully diluted, the incident is framed as a "sober reality of the new AI paradigm". Coinkite is now seemingly just a victim of this new reality, not someone who fucked up in an insane way and takes full responsibility for that. Coinkite had one job, build a product that provides sufficient entropy. They failed in such a spectacular way, and for such a long periode of time, that their users are now suffering the ultimate loss in Bitcoin. The "new AI paradigm" they describe as the culprit, cannot cannot overcome 128 bits of properly generated entropy. It's therefore extremely disappointing (but sadly expected) to see this kind of diversions in an apology post while the catastrophic losses of their users are still mounting.
